text:
anna: Heads up — after yesterday's RBAC rollout we started seeing intermittent SCIM deprovision failures hitting 503s from Okta and a bunch of KMS decrypt errors in the logs. Can someone triage?

sam: On it. Can you paste a correlation id / sample log line? Also, which customers are impacted?

anna: Sample from scim-proxy: 
```
2026-03-20T21:14:02Z ERROR scim-proxy request_id=8f7c1e9a user=svc-account-42 status=503 upstream_error="okta 503"
2026-03-20T21:14:02Z ERROR kms-client decrypt failed request_id=8f7c1e9a error="jwe: envelope header mismatch"
```
Affected: 5 customers so far (enterprise tier) — customer-ids put in #support.

maria: We rotated the KMS key alias this morning during the maintenance window (alias/redwood/primary -> alias/redwood/primary-v2). Did the RBAC change also modify any service-account external IDs?

anna: Yes, RBAC change removed the old `scim-service` role from a couple of service accounts as part of entitlement cleanup. Might correlate.

devops: We also shipped rbac-service 1.9.0 at 21:00 UTC (canary -> prod). Change-log: revert of legacy role inheritance + tighter SCIM permissions. Link: https://ci.redwood/12345

security-bot: alert: audit-ingest pipeline detected missing `scim.deprovision` entries for 7 distinct account_ids in the last 2 hours. Sink backlog growing.

jon: Two parallel failure modes to check: (1) SCIM attempt fails because KMS decryption of the service account extid fails (envelope header mismatch) and code bails before emitting audit, (2) SCIM request reaches Okta but Okta returns 503 and we drop audit on transient errors.

sam: Good breakdown. Steps I'll run: (A) query KMS logs for decrypt errors around 21:00-21:20 UTC for that request_id, (B) check deploy history for rbac-service and feature flags, (C) inspect audit sink for dropped messages.

maria: Quick note: the alias rename created a secondary key material ARN behind the alias for v2; if some services still reference the previous alias string in env configs they will fail to decrypt new envelopes. Search for `alias/redwood/primary` references — I suspect scim-proxy uses the old env var.

anna: I grep'd scim-proxy config: two pods still have env KMS_ALIAS=alias/redwood/primary, others point to alias/redwood/primary-v2.

devops: Rolling restart those two pods now. Running: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/scim-proxy -n infra` -> started.

okta-bot: Provisioning event for customer-foo: request_id=8f7c1e9a status=503 okta_error=temporarily_unavailable retry-after=30s

jon: While the pods restart, we should not rotate/roll keys. We need to backfill audit for the window and requeue failed SCIM events. If KMS encryption envelopes used v2 material but service tried to decrypt with v1, re-encrypting payloads with v2 key (or restoring alias) will be needed.

sam: Agreed. I'm pausing any further RBAC rollouts. @maria can you confirm whether the envelope headers for those failed decrypts indicate v1 or v2? If v1, we can point alias back temporarily.

maria: Looked at raw KMS logs — headers show key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-v2 (so v2). But failing decrypt attempts are from pods referencing `alias/redwood/primary` which still maps to old key-id. That explains envelope mismatch.

anna: OK that matches. Action: revert alias mapping to point `alias/redwood/primary` -> key/abcd-v2 while we finish rollout. @devops can you apply?

devops: I won't change alias mapping without approval from security. Aliases are sensitive. Proposing alternative: restart pods so they pick up env var update to `alias/redwood/primary-v2` (faster), then re-run backfill. We already restarted the two pods — showing healthy.

jon: Restart + backfill seems safest. Avoid alias flips that can cause transient decrypt errors elsewhere.

sam: OK do restart + backfill. I'll queue the backfill job but we need to ensure audit replay keeps ordering. Backfill command: 
```
# replay failed scim events from dead-letter queue
python tools/replay_scim_backfill.py --since 2026-03-20T20:45:00Z --dry-run
```
I'll run dry-run then execute after signoff.

anna: After restarts pods are green, no new 503s seen in the last 3 mins for those customers.

security-bot: runbook-check: scim-provisioning incident template v1.2 applied. Current severity: P2.

maria: Please hold on backfill until I confirm no other services reference the old alias. Running a cluster-wide grep for `alias/redwood/primary` now.

devops: ETA 10m. Also flagged the rbac-service deploy for rollback in case permission removal caused any side-effect hooks.

sam: I'll coordinate with support to notify affected customers (brief status update + ETA for fix). Also adding trace of request_id 8f7c1e9a to the incident ticket.

anna: Thanks all. After we finish backfill we should run an audit verification: ensure `scim.deprovision` events exist for those account_ids and a matching entry in the KMS-access logs.

jon: Postmortem items penciled: (1) alias change protocol docs + canary checks, (2) RBAC change smoke tests for SCIM service accounts, (3) make audit emit resilient to KMS decrypt failures (emit placeholder + retry) so we don't lose audit on transient crypto issues.

maria: Found one more pod in a different cluster still using old alias — patched env var and restarted.

okta-bot: okta provisioning retry for request_id=8f7c1e9a succeeded after 2nd attempt status=200

anna: Great. Sam, can you confirm backfill run and close the incident once audits verified?

sam: Will do. Running replay (not dry-run) now. Will post results here in ~8m. :thumbsup:

security-bot: reminder: please attach all relevant log snippets and KMS audit entries to the ticket for compliance review.

anna: attaching logs to ticket shortly. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
